twin_model.primitives package

SimPy Primitives Framework for Ontology-Driven Virtual Twin.

This module provides generic building blocks (primitives) that compose into complex manufacturing systems. Primitives emit rich observables for discovery-based learning without prescriptive mappings.

class twin_model.primitives.BasePrimitive(env, config, sampling_config=None)[source]

Bases: ABC

Base class for all SimPy primitives.

All primitives must emit observables for discovery-based learning. This base class provides core functionality for: - Observable emission and storage - Configuration management - SimPy environment integration - Common event patterns

The observable stream is the primary mechanism through which the LLM discovers relationships and patterns without prescriptive rules.

emit_observable(event_type, details, severity='INFO')[source]

Emit an observable event with sampling and performance optimization.

This is the primary mechanism for primitives to communicate their state and behavior. Events are now sampled based on configuration to prevent memory exhaustion in long simulations.

Parameters:

  • event_type (str) – Type of event (state_change, production, failure, etc.)

  • details (Dict[str, Any]) – Event-specific details with rich context

  • severity (str) – Event severity (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL)

Return type:

None

class twin_model.primitives.EquipmentPrimitive(env, config, upstream=None, downstream=None, sampling_config=None)[source]

Bases: BasePrimitive

Generic equipment that processes materials.

Emits rich observables for pattern discovery including: - State transitions with context (buffer levels, runtime, product) - Production events with quality metrics - Failure events with contributing factors - Performance variations by shift/product - Energy consumption patterns - Cascade failure propagation

  • config (PrimitiveConfig) – Equipment configuration containing: - base_rate: Units per minute nominal capacity - mtbf: Mean time between failures in minutes - mttr: Mean time to repair in minutes - energy_consumption_rate: kWh per minute when running
